decisions: The policy is the minimal one (a1): FabricSurface takes MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE by default, in its constructor, in the pattern of GodotAccessibleView's constructor; a scene may override it.

The world listens to the mouse stream, emulated mouse included, and counts but does not act on ScreenTouch; a game that needs multi-touch listens to ScreenTouch and skips events whose device is DEVICE_ID_EMULATION.
The wheel over the empty area already reaches the world with a STOP Surface (Control.force_pass_scroll_events is true by default), so its checks are plain checks and not normative.
The mouse wheel over a tree overlay still reaches the world: it is an informative gap; the Modal blocks all four inputs.
The hit slop, a Text with onPress, the gaps of a ScrollView and the wheel over the HUD are informative rows, left to slice 2 (variant a2, after PR #58).
The probe's two sabotages are applied by the probe, so no host is rebuilt; the previous-host control swaps the preserved dylib and restores it byte for byte.

goNoGo.reading: Slice 1 of 3: GO for the minimal policy (a1). A click on the HUD's empty area reaches the map exactly once, a Pressable is pressed once and never reaches the map, and with a tree overlay or a Modal open nothing does, in both topologies, under load, on a real window with the native renderer. The go/no-go itself is decided in slice 3, on the numbers of slices 1 and 2.
goNoGo.timeBox: 3 slices: 1 = this one (minimal policy and the measurement of what it leaves open); 2 = variant a2 for the open cases, after PR #58; 3 = the decision.

limitations: Local macOS arm64 evidence; hosted CI is pending.
The events are synthetic, delivered through Input.parse_input_event: no hardware pointer, no real touch screen, no multi-touch (a second finger), no drag.
No Godot mobile export and no iPhone run: the iphone criterion of V05-02 stays open (package P7).
A hit slop, a Text with onPress, the gaps of a ScrollView and the mouse wheel over the HUD or over a tree overlay still reach the world as well as React Native; they are recorded, not judged.
The scene has the world before the HUD's CanvasLayer in the tree and a Camera2D at (384, 256) with zoom 2; other arrangements are not measured.
The counts are exact and say nothing about latency or frame time.
The windowed lane ran on the Compatibility renderer of an Apple M3 Pro with synthetic events; the captures are an 800 x 600 readback of the root viewport.
